title: Sunny and the Baby Wombat
description: Little Sonny the quokka meets a round, sleepy baby wombat on a quiet afternoon. A warm, cosy bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
One afternoon, Sunny was sitting quietly beneath the shady paperback tree, watching the light move through the leaves.

That was when he heard it.

A soft, shuffling sound. And then a small round shape appeared from behind a log — a baby wombat, grey and plump and moving with the slowest, most contented walk Sunny had ever seen.

The baby wombat didn't seem to notice Sunny at all. It was too busy sniffing the ground, taking small, careful steps, exploring its little patch of the world.

Sunny watched with a smile.

The baby wombat found a patch of soft grass and sniffed it thoroughly. Then it turned in a slow circle. Then it sat down with a small thump and looked around, blinking its deep dark eyes.

Then it noticed Sunny.

They looked at each other for a long, quiet moment.

Sunny gave a very small wave.

The baby wombat blinked again, then waddled a few steps closer. It sniffed in Sunny's direction. Then it sat down again, right beside the base of the tree, tucked its legs in neatly, and rested its broad grey head on the ground.

Just like that. Comfortable. Decided. Asleep in moments.

Sunny looked at the sleeping wombat with the softest feeling in his chest.

He leaned back against the tree and listened to the afternoon sounds — the leaves, the distant creek, the high sweet call of a honeyeater somewhere in the branches above.

His own eyes grew heavy.

The baby wombat breathed in and out, slow and steady, like a little grey tide.

Sunny closed his eyes too.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, baby wombat. Goodnight, soft and sleepy afternoon.
